question: Consider a quadrilateral \(ABCD\) in the \(XY\)-plane with all of its angles less than \(180^\circ\). Let \(P\) be an arbitrary point in the plane and consider the six triangles each of which is formed by the point \(P\) and two of the points \(A,B,C,D\). Then the total area of these six triangles is minimum when the point \(P\) is

options.B: one of the vertices of the quadrilateral
options.C: intersection of the diagonals of the quadrilateral
options.D: none of the points given in (A), (B) or (C).
